name: MLOps Interview Prep
subject: mlops
description: CI/CD for ML, model registries, feature stores, monitoring

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Feature Store in an MLOps pipeline?
options: To store trained model weights
To provide consistent, reusable feature computation for training and serving
To schedule model retraining jobs
To log model predictions in production
questions.explanation: A Feature Store ensures the same feature logic runs at training time and serving time, eliminating training-serving skew.

questions.question: Which metric would you monitor first to detect data drift in a production ML model?
options: GPU utilization
Statistical distribution of input features over time
Number of API requests per minute
Model binary size
questions.explanation: Monitoring input feature distributions (PSI, KL divergence) detects data drift before it degrades model performance.

questions.question: What does a Model Registry primarily store?
options: Raw training datasets
Versioned model artifacts, metadata, and lineage
Feature definitions and transformations
CI/CD pipeline configurations
questions.explanation: A Model Registry tracks versioned model artifacts with metadata like metrics, parameters, and lineage.

questions.question: In a canary deployment for an ML model, what controls the traffic split between old and new model?
options: Feature store routing rules
A load balancer or service mesh weighted routing
The model accuracy threshold
Number of GPUs available
questions.explanation: Traffic splitting in canary release is managed at the infrastructure layer via a service mesh or load balancer.

questions.question: What is the key difference between online and offline feature serving in a Feature Store?
options: Offline serving uses GPUs; online uses CPUs
Online serving provides low-latency lookups for inference; offline provides batch data for training
Offline serving is encrypted; online is not
Online features are computed weekly; offline features are computed in real time
questions.explanation: Online stores (Redis) serve features in milliseconds for inference. Offline stores (S3, BigQuery) serve historical data for training.

questions.question: What is 'model decay' (also called concept drift)?
options: The model file becomes corrupted over time
Model performance degrades because the real-world data distribution changed from training data
The model's inference speed slows after many requests
Memory leaks in the model serving container
questions.explanation: Concept drift: the statistical relationship between input features and the target label changes over time, degrading model accuracy.

questions.question: What is the purpose of shadow deployment (shadow mode) for an ML model?
options: Serving the new model to internal users only
Running the new model in parallel with production but discarding its predictions
Deploying the model to a backup cluster
Testing the model offline before any deployment
questions.explanation: In shadow mode, the new model processes all real traffic but its predictions are logged, not served. Allows comparison without user impact.

questions.question: Which tool is most commonly used for ML experiment tracking?
options: Jenkins
MLflow
Terraform
Prometheus
questions.explanation: MLflow tracks experiments, parameters, metrics, and artifacts. Alternatives include Weights & Biases and Neptune.

questions.question: What is 'training-serving skew' in ML systems?
options: The model trains faster than it serves
The features at serving time differ from the features used during training
Different hardware between training and serving
Version mismatch between Python and model library
questions.explanation: Training-serving skew: if feature preprocessing differs between training and inference, predictions degrade silently.

questions.question: What does 'model serving latency P99' measure?
options: The average response time across all requests
The response time below which 99% of requests fall
The time to train the model from scratch
99% of the model's predictions being correct
questions.explanation: P99 latency is the 99th percentile — 99% of requests are faster than this. It captures tail latency, which matters for user experience.

questions.question: What is Kubeflow's primary use case?
options: Storing ML datasets in cloud storage
Orchestrating ML workflows on Kubernetes
Monitoring model drift in production
Hyperparameter tuning only
questions.explanation: Kubeflow is an ML toolkit for Kubernetes — it handles pipelines, training operators, model serving, and hyperparameter tuning.

questions.question: What is A/B testing for ML models?
options: Testing model A on CPU and model B on GPU
Splitting real traffic between two model versions and comparing their performance
Running two training jobs with different datasets
Comparing offline evaluation metrics of two models
questions.explanation: A/B testing routes a fraction of real traffic to each model version and measures production metrics (CTR, revenue, accuracy) to pick the winner.

questions.question: What is the role of a data validation step in an ML pipeline?
options: Compresses training data for faster loading
Detects schema mismatches, outliers, and distribution anomalies before training
Converts data to model-readable binary format
Splits data into train/test sets
questions.explanation: Data validation (using tools like TFX or Great Expectations) catches data quality issues early, preventing silent model degradation.

questions.question: What is model quantization?
options: Measuring model performance with multiple metrics
Reducing model size by converting weights from float32 to int8 or float16
Adding more quantitative features to the model
Setting a quality threshold for model deployment
questions.explanation: Quantization compresses model weights (float32→int8) to reduce inference latency and memory footprint with minimal accuracy loss.

questions.question: What does 'continuous training' (CT) mean in MLOps?
options: Training the model 24/7 without stopping
Automatically retraining the model when new data arrives or drift is detected
Using continuous integration for training code
Training on a continuously growing dataset
questions.explanation: CT automatically triggers model retraining based on data freshness or performance degradation signals, keeping the model up-to-date.

questions.question: Which format is most common for serving ML models via REST API?
options: CSV
Pickle
ONNX or TensorFlow SavedModel
Jupyter notebook
questions.explanation: ONNX (cross-framework) and TensorFlow SavedModel are production serving formats. Pickle is insecure and not portable.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a feature pipeline vs a training pipeline in MLOps?
options: They are the same pipeline
Feature pipelines compute and store features; training pipelines use those features to train models
Feature pipelines handle raw data only; training pipelines handle labels
Training pipelines run in batch; feature pipelines run only in real-time
questions.explanation: Separating feature and training pipelines decouples feature freshness from training schedules, enabling feature reuse across multiple models.

questions.question: What does BentoML provide in an MLOps stack?
options: Data labeling and annotation
A framework-agnostic way to package, serve, and deploy ML models
Distributed model training
Hyperparameter optimization
questions.explanation: BentoML packages ML models with their dependencies and APIs into portable 'bentos' that can be deployed to any cloud or container platform.

questions.question: What is the 'Four Pillars' model evaluation framework for production ML?
options: Accuracy, Speed, Cost, Simplicity
Data quality, Model quality, System reliability, Business impact
Training, Evaluation, Deployment, Monitoring
Bias, Variance, Overfitting, Underfitting
questions.explanation: Production ML evaluation considers all four: data quality (garbage in), model quality (metrics), system reliability (uptime), and business impact (ROI).

questions.question: What does 'model lineage' track in a Model Registry?
options: The ancestry of training data sources, code versions, and hyperparameters that produced the model
How many times a model has been called in production
The model's accuracy trend over time
The list of engineers who trained the model
questions.explanation: Lineage tracks: which dataset, code version, and parameters produced a model version — enabling reproducibility and audit.
